candidate.answerReason: The given powers imply \(60^{1-a-b}=4\) and \(60^{1-b}=12\). Substituting the latter into the expression reduces it to \(\sqrt4=2\).

methods.label: Rewrite the base as a power of 60
methods.explanation:
The combinations \(1-a-b\) and \(1-b\) suggest dividing the known powers of 60. The exponent laws give
\[
60^{1-a-b}=\frac{60}{60^a60^b}
=\frac{60}{3\cdot5}=4
\]
and
\[
60^{1-b}=\frac{60}{60^b}=12.
\]
The second equality also shows that \(1-b\ne0\), since a zero exponent would give 1 rather than 12. We can therefore substitute \(60^{1-b}\) for the base 12 and cancel the matching exponent factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
12^{\frac{1-a-b}{2(1-b)}}
&=\left(60^{1-b}\right)^{\frac{1-a-b}{2(1-b)}}\\
&=60^{(1-a-b)/2}\\
&=\sqrt{60^{1-a-b}}\\
&=\sqrt4=\boxed{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All bases are positive, so these real-exponent laws apply. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
